solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Recovering from mixed gin espressos

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the two drinks are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone getting over a hangover caused by an odd cocktail of gin and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recovering' looks like getting better, but here it means taking goods back from a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bailiffs reclaiming goods on unpaid credit are taking them back, a sense of recovering property.

clue.text: Hard, finding clubs in New York

indicators.note: in says the clubs letter goes inside the rearranged York
New suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of York

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Something tough discovered at a golf or night club in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' reads as the city, but 'New' is the anagram signal for York, giving ROKY, with C put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky ground is stony and difficult, so the adjective serves as a synonym of difficult or tough.

clue.text: Overseeing helper?

parts.note: read as 'over-seeing': a device that lets a submarine crew see over the surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overseeing' suggests a supervisor's assistant; split it as over-seeing and it is an instrument for looking over things.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's tube of mirrors lets viewers look above an obstruction or the waterline.

clue.text: Sarah giving a speech to relish

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
addressing an audience means speaking to it

explanation.surface: Sarah delivers a talk with great enthusiasm and enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a verb for enjoying; it is the noun for a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a sauce or condiment, and a vinaigrette poured over leaves is one such accompaniment.

clue.text: Finale cut short before middle part: we want more!

indicators.note: before places the shortened word ahead of the middle part
cut short means the last letter of the word is chopped off

parts.note: the end is the finale
the core is the central part

explanation.surface: An audience at the close of a show, cut off midway, shouting for more.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience calls out this French word when demanding an extra piece after the performance.

clue.text: Mad piranhas as terrible as fleet of warships

indicators.note: terrible says these letters are mangled into a different order

explanation.surface: A comparison: crazed piranhas are as fearsome as a naval invasion force.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1588 Spanish invasion force of galleons sent against England is the famous historic naval fleet.

clue.text: Nothing left in back

indicators.note: back says the letters are read from the end towards the start

explanation.surface: Nothing has been left at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: L and IN make LIN, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is a score of zero, as in sports results, so it means none at all.

clue.text: Tune from mass organised yodel

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: organised means the letters of yodel are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A song produced by a big group of people yodelling together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a sequence of musical notes, which is exactly what a melody is.

clue.text: Sea creature caught by mouth

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
oral means relating to the mouth

explanation.surface: A marine animal is seized in someone's jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is made of tiny marine polyps, animals that build reefs in the ocean.

clue.text: Silly fellow to singe pork pie

parts.note: to char is to scorch or singe
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie (porky)

explanation.surface: A daft man is told to burn a meat pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' looks like food; in British rhyming slang it means a lie, often shortened to 'porky'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a fool or idiot, as in 'a right charlie'.

clue.text: Some sockeye salmon? Certainly!

indicators.note: Some says only part of the words sockeye salmon is wanted, letters lying within them

explanation.surface: Asked whether to have some fish, someone replies emphatically in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic affirmative reply; both words express agreement.

clue.text: Blundering into strange turning, showing adventurous spirit

indicators.note: into says the blundering word goes inside the other
turning says the word for strange is read backwards

parts.note: odd means strange
erring means making mistakes, blundering

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into an unfamiliar bend, displaying boldness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blundering' looks like the anagram signal for 'into'; it is the synonym that goes inside, and 'strange turning' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic daring or reckless courage, the stuff of swashbuckling tales.

clue.text: Rabat girl moved somewhere just north of her country

definitions.text: somewhere just north of her country

indicators.note: moved says the letters are shifted into another order

explanation.surface: A girl from Rabat in Morocco relocated to a nearby place across the strait.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabat is the capital of Morocco, and the Rock lies just across the strait to its north.
explanation.definitionFit: The British territory at Spain's tip sits a few miles north of Morocco across the strait.

clue.text: Look in thick hair for fine powder

indicators.note: in puts the word for look inside the word for hair

parts.note: fur is an animal's thick hair
lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Someone searching a thick mane for traces of powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground grain used for baking is a fine dry meal.

clue.text: Pointless empty unit in document holder

indicators.note: in places the emptied unit inside the file

parts.note: a file holds documents

indicators.note: empty means the word unit loses its inner letters, keeping only the first and last

explanation.surface: A useless, empty component found inside a folder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile is useless, serving no purpose or achieving nothing.

clue.text: Falcon's pursuit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pastime or leisure activity

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests a falcon's hunting; the 's merely joins two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small bird of prey and an activity done for pleasure in spare time.

clue.text: Barrister's underpants

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister in Britain is a courtroom lawyer who receives instructions called briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the legal instructions a lawyer takes on and short undergarments.

clue.text: Change of rate more certain for financial official

indicators.note: Change of says the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A change in the interest rate gives a finance officer more confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who manages a club's or society's money and accounts holds this post.

clue.text: Not totally against insect

indicators.note: Not totally means the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: Someone only partly opposed to a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The creature is a small social insect living in colonies.

clue.text: Chuck half of this paddle

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters of this are kept

parts.note: to row is to paddle a boat

explanation.surface: Toss away half of this oar.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck something is to toss or hurl it.

clue.text: Tactile woven mesh

indicators.note: woven suggests the letters are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: A net woven so it feels pleasant to the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework of strips, a kind of open grid or net.

clue.text: Regularly strokes digit

indicators.note: Regularly says every other letter of strokes is taken, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone repeatedly caresses a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' suggests a finger; here it is one on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits include toes as well as fingers, the jointed extremities of feet.

clue.text: Undergo conversion in church structure, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is the one that sounds like the church structure

parts.note: an altar is the communion table in a church

explanation.surface: Being converted to a faith at a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to change, intransitively as well, so it means become different.

clue.text: Limits phosphorus in agricultural device for small bird

indicators.note: in puts the limits and phosphorus inside the farm implement

parts.note: a harrow is a farm implement for breaking up soil
edges are limits or borders
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: Restrictions on phosphorus fertiliser in farm machinery, all for a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The tempting split gives HEDGES for 'Limits', but then nothing is left to hold the phosphorus; the farm implement must wrap around instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock, a small brown garden songbird, is also called the hedge sparrow.
